heroHeadline: Lebanon-Israel Round 3 Washington Talks Underway as Ceasefire Expires May 17; US Congress Moves to Block Any Iran Enrichment Deal
heroSubtitle: May 14–15, 2026 sees two decisive developments in global peace diplomacy. The third round of direct Lebanon-Israel negotiations opened at the U.S. State Department on May 14 and continues May 15 — described by a U.S. official as 'productive, positive' — with the April 16 ceasefire framework expiring May 17, making a ceasefire extension agreement the most urgent deliverable. The talks involve Lebanese envoy Simon Karam, Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter, IDF Brig.-Gen. Amichai Levin, and U.S. facilitators including Secretary Rubio directly. The fundamental impasse persists: Israel conditions withdrawal on Hezbollah disarmament south of the Litani; Lebanon insists on unconditional IDF withdrawal first. If Round 3 fails to produce a ceasefire extension, Lebanon faces a political crisis — with Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem continuing to demand Lebanon abandon the Washington direct format. On the Iran track, a bipartisan group of 52 U.S. senators and 177 representatives wrote to President Trump on May 14 opposing any nuclear deal permitting Iran to continue uranium enrichment on its own soil — effectively eliminating the 12-15 year enrichment duration compromise that negotiators Witkoff and Kushner had been exploring. This narrows the US-Iran MOU space to an absolute demand that Iran has already called an existential red line. UN Gaza peace envoy Nikolay Mladenov separately warned May 14 that Gaza risks permanent partition if Phase 2 negotiations (Hamas disarmament, governance transition) do not advance, as the U.S. begins implementing a 'Plan B' framework in non-Hamas controlled areas ahead of a June rollout.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN, African Union, IGAD, Crisis Group, USIP, PA-X Database, and Tier 1–3 sources across all media poles.
